records.name: Umayyad Caliphate · Islam
records.summary: Islam is mapped as the ruling dynasty’s religious affiliation, using the dated polity’s approximate claimed/controlled extent. It does not imply a Muslim majority in every province. 750 is a transition year; the annual source polygon cannot distinguish phases within that year.

records.name: Byzantine Empire · Christianity
records.summary: Christianity was the state religion of the culturally and religiously diverse Byzantine Empire. This broad period begins after the late-fourth-century establishment described by the source. It does not erase doctrinal disputes or identify every resident’s belief.

records.name: India · Hindu majority, Census 2011
records.summary: The 2011 national census reported 79.8% Hindu affiliation. This is a country-level census result for that observation year, not a local majority everywhere and not a declaration of state religion. Census enumeration coverage differs from some claimed-border polygons; the map is a national aggregate proxy. It is not carried into later years.

met-umayyad.author: Department of Islamic Art, Metropolitan Museum of Art
met-umayyad.locator: Umayyad dynasty and Islamic rule; explicitly describes religiously diverse lands. Original factual summary only.

met-byzantium.title: Byzantium (ca. 330–1453)
met-byzantium.author: Metropolitan Museum of Art
met-byzantium.locator: Christian state and late-fourth-century establishment of Christianity as official religion in a diverse empire.

india-census-release.author: Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India / Press Information Bureau, 2015
